verses.zh: 你们要赞美耶和华！你们要赞美耶和华的名！耶和华的仆人站在耶和华殿中；站在我们　神殿院中的，你们要赞美他！
verses.en: Praise the Lord.Praise the name of the Lord.Offer praise, you servants of the Lord,
verses.commentary:
135:1 "Praise" This is the Hebrew term "Hallelujah." Notice the name for Israel's Deity is the abbreviated
YHWH—Yah (Ps. 135:1,3,4,21), which forms the end of praise (lit. Praise the Lord).

▣ "the name of the Lord" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" of YHWH.

verses.zh: a
verses.en: who serve[NOTE:1] in the Lord’s temple,in the courts of the temple of our God.
notes: Psalm 135. The psalmist urges God’s people to praise him because he is the incomparable God and ruler of the world who has accomplished great things for Israel.

verses.zh: 你们要赞美耶和华！耶和华本为善；要歌颂他的名，因为这是美好的。
verses.en: Praise the Lord, for the Lord is good.Sing praises to his name, for it is pleasant.[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 耶和华拣选雅各归自己，拣选以色列特作自己的子民。
verses.en: Indeed,[NOTE:1] the Lord has chosen Jacob for himself,Israel to be his special possession.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for [it is] pleasant.” The translation assumes that it is the Lord’s “name” that is pleasant. Another option is to understand the referent of “it” as the act of praising (see Ps 147:1).

verses.zh: 原来我知道耶和华为大，也知道我们的主超乎万神之上。
verses.en: Yes,[NOTE:1] I know the Lord is great,and our Lord is superior to all gods.
notes: His special possession. The language echoes Exod 19:5; Deut 7:6; 14:2; 26:18. See also Mal 3:17.
verses.commentary:
135:5 "I know" See SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

▣ "Lord" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

135:5b "Lord" This is the Hebrew Adon, which means "master," "owner," "husband," or "Lord."

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD (Adon and Kurios)

▣ "our Lord is above all gods" YHWH is the only God (cf. Exod. 18:11; Ps. 95:3; 96:4; 97:9). This is
where the exclusivisim of Israel is very obvious! She was the only monotheistic nation of the ANE.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

verses.zh: 耶和华在天上，在地下，在海中，在一切的深处，都随自己的意旨而行。
verses.en: He does whatever he pleasesin heaven and on earth,in the seas and all the ocean depths.
verses.commentary:
135:6 "Whatever the Lord please, He does" This is a strong
statement on the sovereignty and complete freedom of YHWH to control and act in His Creation. A good
example would be Isa. 55:9-11.

▣ "In heaven and in earth, in the seas" This is typical language for creation (i.e., this planet, cf. Exod. 20:11;
Neh. 9:6; Ps. 69:34; 96:11; 146:6; Hag. 2:6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

▣ "the seas. . .all deeps" These may be synonymous or the first of YHWH's control of (1) agricultural
water (i.e., rain, dew in their season) and (2) water as a weapon (i.e., lightning, floods, plagues, etc.). The second
may refer to the imagery of ANE mythology of YHWH defeating watery chaos (cf. Ps 65:5-7; 89:9-10; Job 26:12-13; Isa. 51:9-10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WATERS

verses.zh: 他使云雾从地极上腾，造电随雨而闪，从府库中带出风来。
verses.en: He causes the clouds to arise from the end of the earth,makes lightning bolts accompany the rain,and brings the wind out of his storehouses.
verses.commentary:
135:7 "His treasuries" This Hebrew NOUN can mean "treasury" or "storehouse." The
OT often uses the imagery of weather phenomena (i.e., hail, snow, wind, lightning, rain/flood) kept in heavenly
storehouses to be used by YHWH, not Ba'al.

- Deut. 28:12

- Job 38:22

- Ps. 33:7

- Jer. 10:13; 51:16

YHWH controls the forces of nature for His purposes (cf. Lev. 26:4-5,9,16,19,22,26; Deut. 27:3;
28:4-5,8,11,12,17-18,22,24,38-42).

verses.zh: 他将埃及头生的，连人带牲畜都击杀了。
verses.en: He struck down the firstborn of Egypt,including both men and animals.
verses.commentary:
135:8 "He smote" This VERB (BDB 645, KB 697, Hiphil PERFECT)
denotes a complete destruction sent and accomplished by God.

- Ps. 135:8 ‒ YHWH's promised deliverance from Egypt (cf. Gen. 15:12-15; Exod. 3:20; 7:25; 9:15; 12:13; Ps. 87:4; Isa. 30:7)

- Ps. 135:10 ‒ YHWH's defeat of the nations of Canaan (cf. Gen. 15:16-21)

verses.zh: 埃及啊，他施行神迹奇事，在你当中，在法老和他一切臣仆身上。
verses.en: He performed awesome deeds[NOTE:1] and acts of judgment[NOTE:2] in your midst, O Egypt,against Pharaoh and all his servants.
verses.commentary:
135:9 "signs and wonders" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SIGNS

verses.zh: 他击杀许多的民，又杀戮大能的王，
verses.en: He defeated many nations,and killed mighty kings—

verses.zh: 就是亚摩利王西宏和巴珊王噩，并迦南一切的国王，
verses.en: Sihon, king of the Amorites,and Og, king of Bashan,and all the kingdoms of Canaan.
verses.commentary:
135:11 Lists of the nations YHWH defeated in the Exodus, Wilderness Wandering, and Conquest of Canaan follow.

- Amorites ‒ Num. 21:2126; Deut. 29:7;
SPECIAL TOPIC: AMORITE

- Bashan ‒ Num. 21:33-35

- Canaanite tribes ‒
SPECIAL TOPIC: PRE-ISRAELITE INHABITANTS OF PALESTINE

verses.zh: 将他们的地赏赐他的百姓以色列为业。
verses.en: He gave their land as an inheritance,as an inheritance to Israel his people.
verses.commentary: 135:12 "He gave their land as a heritage" This is mentioned in YHWH's vision to Abraham in Gen. 15:12-21.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你的名存到永远！耶和华啊，你可记念的名存到万代！
verses.en: O Lord, your name endures,[NOTE:1] your reputation, O Lord, lasts.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “portents”; “omens” (see Ps 71:7). The Egyptian plagues are alluded to here.
verses.commentary:
135:13 "Your name, O Lord" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: "'THE NAME" OF YHWH

▣ "everlasting" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam). This may be a play on the root meaning of YHWH from the Hebrew
VERB "to be." YHWH is the only living, ever living Being. All life comes from Him and is sustained by Him.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣

NASB
"Your remembrance"

NKJV, JPSOA
"Your fame"

NRSV, REB, LXX
"Your renown"

NJB
"Your memory"

The Hebrew NOUN (BDB 271) means "remembrance" or "memorial."

- human's memory ‒ Prov. 10:7; Eccl. 9:5

- Israel ‒ Hos.14:7

- YHWH ‒ Exod. 3:15; Ps. 6:6; 30:4; 97:12; 102:12; Isa. 26:8; Hosea 12:5

verses.zh: 耶和华要为他的百姓伸冤，为他的仆人后悔。
verses.en: For the Lord vindicates[NOTE:1] his peopleand has compassion on his servants.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “O Lord, your remembrance [is] for a generation and a generation.” See Ps 102:12.
Heb “judges,” but here the idea is that the Lord “judges on behalf of” his people. The imperfect verbal forms here and in the next line draw attention to the Lord’s characteristic actions.
verses.commentary: 135:14 For a good parallel passage, see Deuteronomy 32:36.

verses.zh: 外邦的偶像是金的，银的，是人手所造的；
verses.en: The nations’ idols are made of silver and gold;they are man-made.[NOTE:1]
notes: Verse 14 echoes Deut 32:36, where Moses affirms that God mercifully relents from fully judging his wayward people.
verses.commentary:
135:15-18 Those who make the idols and then worship them will be like them.

- cannot speak

- cannot see

- cannot hear

- cannot breathe

They are lifeless imaginations of fallen, false human hearts and hands. Idols cannot help or know,
so too, the worshipers (cf. Ps. 97:7; Isa. 42:17; 44:5-17; 45:16; 46:7; Jer. 10:2-16; Hab. 2:18)!

verses.zh: 有口却不能言，有眼却不能看，
verses.en: They have mouths, but cannot speak,eyes, but cannot see,

verses.zh: 有耳却不能听，口中也没有气息。
verses.en: and ears, but cannot hear.Indeed, they cannot breathe.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the work of the hands of man.”

verses.zh: 造他的要和他一样，凡靠他的也要如此。
verses.en: Those who make them will end up[NOTE:1] like them,as will everyone who trusts in them.
notes: Heb “indeed, there is not breath in their mouth.” For the collocation אַף אֵין (ʾaf ʾen, “indeed, there is not”) see Isa 41:26. Another option is to take אַף as “nose” (see Ps 115:6), in which case one might translate, “a nose, [but] they have no breath in their mouths.”

verses.zh: 以色列家啊，你们要称颂耶和华！亚伦家啊，你们要称颂耶和华！
verses.en: O family[NOTE:1] of Israel, praise the Lord.O family of Aaron, praise the Lord.
notes: Heb “will be.” Another option is to take the prefixed verbal form as a prayer, “may those who make them end up like them.” sn Because the idols are lifeless, they cannot help their worshipers in times of crisis. Consequently the worshipers end up as dead as the gods in which they trust.
verses.commentary:
135:19 This refers to

- all the tribes of Israel

- the special tribe of Levi, family of Aaron, YHWH's choice for His temple servants to come from In a sense,
this tribe replaced the firstborn children of all the tribes as YHWH's servants (cf. Exodus 13).

verses.zh: 利未家啊，你们要称颂耶和华！你们敬畏耶和华的，要称颂耶和华！
verses.en: O family of Levi, praise the Lord.You loyal followers[NOTE:1] of the Lord, praise the Lord.
notes: Heb “house” (here and in the next two lines).
verses.commentary:
135:20 "house of Levi" Not all Levites were priests but all priests were of the tribe of Levi. Some Levites

- served in the temple (see note at Ps. 134:1)

- served locally as teachers of the Law of Moses

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR and

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

verses.zh: 住在耶路撒冷的耶和华该从锡安受称颂。你们要赞美耶和华！
verses.en: The Lord deserves praise in Zion[NOTE:1]—he who dwells in Jerusalem.[NOTE:2] Praise the Lord.
notes: Heb “praised be the Lord from Zion.”
verses.commentary:
135:21 "Zion" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, JEBUS, SALEM, JERUSALEM, ZION.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- List the characteristics of Israel's God.

- Define monotheism.

- Does God control weather for His purposes? Does that mean God sends all storms, floods, fire, etc.?

- Why is trusting in idols so sad?

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This Psalm starts and concludes with

- praise ‒ BDB 237, KB 248, Piel IMPERATIVE, Ps. 135:1 (thrice), 3a, 21c

- sing ‒ BDB 274, KB 273, Piel IMPERATIVE, Ps. 135:3b

- bless ‒ BDB 138, KB 159, Piel IMPERATIVE, Ps. 135:19 (twice), 20 (twice)

- YHWH is praised/blessed/sung about because

- character

- He is good, Ps. 135:3 (cf. Ps. 147:1)

- He is lovely, Ps. 135:3 (cf. Ps. 27:4; 147:1)

- He is great, Ps. 135:5 (cf. Ps. 48:1; 145:3)

- He is above all gods, Ps. 135:5 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM)

- His name is everlasting, Ps. 135:13a (cf. Exod. 3:15)

- His memory of His promises is sure, Ps. 135:13b

- acts for Israel

- chose Jacob/Israel, Ps. 135:4 (cf. Deut. 7:6; 10:15)

- sovereign, Ps. 135:6 (cf. Ps. 115:3; Eccl. 8:3; Isa. 46:8-10)

- controls water, Ps. 135:7 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS)

- delivered Israel from Egypt, Ps. 135:8-9 (cf. Ps. 136:10-15)

- protected Israel in the wandering period, Ps. 135:10-11 (cf. Ps. 136:16-22)

- His acts toward Israel

- chose them, Ps. 135:4 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US)

- judged them, Ps. 135:14

(1) for their sin (cf. Heb. 10:26-31)

(2) or on their behalf against the nations (cf. Ps. 50:4)

- but will forgive (cf. Ps. 134:14b)

- This Psalm includes a strophe on the folly of idolatry (cf. Ps. 135:14-18). He and He alone is God (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM).
This strophe is similar to Ps. 115:4-8 (also note Exod. 20:23; Deut. 4:28; 29:17).

- Many/most of the phrasing of this Psalm is found in other Scripture texts. The date of the Psalm is uncertain
(i.e., did it quote or was it quoted?).
